subject: Private/VPC — operational scenarios for customer-controlled storage and deletion

Subject: Private/VPC — operational scenarios for customer-controlled storage and deletion

Hi Elena,

Thanks for the list of requirements you sent over this morning. Below is a short mapping of how Redwood handles customer-controlled storage and deletion in Private/VPC deployments, plus pointers to an operational runbook (attached). I tried to keep this focused on the scenarios you flagged: active data residency, customer-managed KMS, deletion/erasure timelines, backups/snaps, and auditability.

High level: in Private/VPC mode customer data (payloads, index/embeddings, cache metadata) is stored on customer-managed storage volumes inside the VPC. Redwood's control plane runs outside the VPC (optional private control plane), but we never persist customer plaintext outside the configured customer volumes.

Key operational scenarios (summary):
- Data residency enforcement: storage lives in customer region; snapshots/volumes inherit region tag.
- Deletion types: soft-delete (mark + 30d grace) vs immediate erasure (zeroing + scrub of KV caches) — configurable per workload via tenant policy.
- Backups/snapshots: scheduled snapshots are retained per the customer retention policy; we provide snapshot manifests and an API to schedule immediate snapshot purge.
- KMS: support for customer-managed keys (CMK) for at-rest encryption; Redwood cannot decrypt without the KMS permissions supplied by the customer.
- Audit & attestation: we can provide deletion proofs (manifest of objects deleted, checksums, and timestamps) and an SOC-style attestation for one-off erasures.

Attached: redwood_vpc_erasure_runbook_v1.pdf — operational steps and command snippets our ops team executes when a customer requests a formal data purge.

Next steps: if you want, we can map these scenarios to specific contract redlines (SLA/retention table) — Marissa, can you take point on drafting the SLA language and the redline?

Best,
Aditya

Elena,

Great questions — answering inline and adding some implementation detail.

1) Deletion proof:
- We can deliver a JSON manifest listing objects removed (object id, path, SHA256, deletion timestamp) plus a short ops attestation signed by our on-call engineer (name, timestamp).
- For KV cache purge: we run a multi-pass scrub (invalidate in-memory cache, then overwrite ephemeral storage, then reindex to ensure no residual references). The runbook has the exact commands and log examples (see attached).

2) Snapshots & DR:
- By default snapshots are stored on volumes inside the VPC. For DR customers who opt into cross-region DR, snapshots are encrypted and pushed to a DR region that you must explicitly enable; we do not enable cross-region snapshot replication by default.
- If cross-region DR is enabled, we provide an allowlist of region targets and require a signed DR activation form (retention & access controls) — we can make that a contractual checkbox.

3) KMS & staff access:
- Yes, we support customer-managed KMS and a "zero-knowledge" path: Redwood control-plane operators cannot decrypt without a one-time KMS grant by the customer. We record and log any KMS grants and can include them in the attestation.

Operational ask: to satisfy Ops, we recommend a pre-production dry-run: Redwood will perform a scripted test erasure on a non-production tenant in your VPC and deliver the deletion manifest and log bundle. Please confirm a target window.

Marissa Cole

Elena / team,

Quick note on backups and snapshots: if you require immediate irrevocable erasure we need to coordinate snapshot purge windows. For example, scheduled daily snapshots have a catalog entry — purge means we delete the snapshot manifest, remove the volume, and run the scrub. That process can take between 1-12 hours depending on volume size.

Edge case: long-term cold backups (customer-managed archival targets) will not be touched unless explicitly included as part of the erasure scope. Please confirm whether archival tiers should be included in the deletion order.

Also looping in Stephanie for a formal attestation sign-off. Stephanie: can we prepare a one-off attestation template and DocuSign flow for Acme?

Thanks,
Karthik
